bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42534620 (freetype): Heap-buffer-overflow READ 8 found by fuzz target fuzz_pdfload [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42534620
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json issue_description / sanitizer_trace.txt / default_crash_trace.txt / reproduction_report.json / staged vulnerable xpdf source
bug_description.normalized: The staged metadata and packaged `patch.diff` are unrelated FreeType artifacts, but Stage 01's saved crash trace and the live ARVO workspace are xpdf 4.05. In `build/fuzz_pdfload.cc`, `FuzzedDataProvider` consumes the last 25 bytes of the 79-byte witness from the end of the buffer before `ConsumeRemainingBytes<char>()`: each `ConsumeFloatingPoint<double>()` takes one `ConsumeBool()` plus 8 probability bytes, `ConsumeIntegral<int>()` takes 4 bytes, and the three explicit `ConsumeBool()` calls take 1 byte each. The remaining first 54 bytes passed to `MemStream` are exactly `35 0 obj<</Pages 30 0R\ntrailer<</Root 35 0R 30 0 obj<<`. In `Catalog::readPageTree`, `catDict->dictLookupNF("Pages", &topPagesRef)` recovers `/Pages 30 0 R` from that catalog object and `topPagesRef.fetch(xref, &topPagesObj)` materializes object 30 as the top Pages node. The referenced object is only `30 0 obj<<` before EOF, so `topPagesObj` has no `/Count`; `topPagesObj.dictLookup("Count", &countObj)->isInt()` fails and xpdf falls back to `numPages = 1`. `readPageTree` then allocates a one-element `pages` array. The fuzz target later executes `for (size_t i = 0; i < doc.getNumPages(); i++)` and calls `doc.getLinks(i)`. On the only iteration `i == 0`, `PDFDoc::getLinks` forwards page 0 to `Catalog::getPage`, which reads `pages[i-1]` without validating the 1-based page number, producing the saved AddressSanitizer heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 8 at `xpdf/Catalog.cc:302`.

source.description: First project-code statement in the closed chain that consumes the attacker-controlled catalog dictionary and materializes the `/Pages` indirect reference used by the vulnerable path.
source.value_from: The saved `poc` is the exact 79-byte `fuzz_pdfload` witness with sha256 `c1dfdfccdff22be50e9114cde2a77f0e55ebcc4bfce13d7a3cb36e67add58bfe`. `FuzzedDataProvider` consumes the last 25 bytes from the end of that buffer before `ConsumeRemainingBytes<char>()` (9 bytes for each `ConsumeFloatingPoint<double>()`, 4 bytes for `ConsumeIntegral<int>()`, then 3 bytes for the explicit `ConsumeBool()` calls), so xpdf receives only the first 54 bytes: `35 0 obj<</Pages 30 0R\ntrailer<</Root 35 0R 30 0 obj<<`. Those 25 consumed bytes are all ASCII spaces (`0x20`), so none of the padding after `30 0 obj<<` reaches xpdf. By the time `Catalog::readPageTree` runs, the catalog dictionary contains the attacker-controlled `/Pages 30 0 R` entry from that prefix, and this statement copies that indirect reference into `topPagesRef`.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer crash site. `Catalog::getPage` subtracts 1 from the supplied page number and dereferences `pages[i-1]` without validating that the caller passed a 1-based index.
sink.note: On the observed crashing path, `i == 0`, so this read becomes `pages[-1]`. ASan reports an 8-byte read 8 bytes to the left of the one-element heap region allocated in `Catalog::readPageTree`.

root_cause.description: Root cause. The fuzz target iterates pages from `i = 0` and passes that zero-based loop value directly to `doc.getLinks(i)`, even though xpdf page accessors are 1-based and `Catalog::getPage` immediately converts them to `pages[i-1]`.
root_cause.note: With the witness-driven fallback `numPages == 1`, this loop executes once with `i == 0`. The very first `doc.getLinks(i)` call already violates the page-number contract before line 101's later `getPage(i)` call could run.

tainted_value_origin.description: This is where the vulnerability-relevant destination extent is created. For the observed path, the fallback page count is `numPages = 1`, so `pages` has exactly one valid slot and any `pages[i-1]` access with `i <= 0` or `i > 1` is out of bounds.

parser_admitted.description: The staged witness is accepted far enough for `PDFDoc doc(stream)` to succeed and `doc.isOk()` to evaluate true, so the harness enters the page-processing loop that later crashes. Stage 01's saved ASan trace from line 100 confirms this checkpoint was reached.

fine_trace.note: Source. `dictLookupNF("Pages", &topPagesRef)` copies the non-fetched `/Pages` value out of the attacker-controlled catalog dictionary. For this witness that value is the indirect reference `30 0 R`, so the `isRef()` guard succeeds and selects object 30 as the top Pages node.

Step 1's `30 0 R` reference is fetched into `topPagesObj`. The referenced bytes are the witness suffix `30 0 obj<<`, so xpdf materializes object 30 as a dictionary and immediately reaches EOF before any key/value pair is added, leaving `topPagesObj` empty.
Because step 2 left `topPagesObj` with no entries, `topPagesObj.dictLookup("Count", &countObj)` does not find `/Count` and initializes a null object, so this `isInt()` test is false.
Because step 3 found no integer `/Count`, xpdf takes the fallback `Page node instead of a Pages node` path and materializes `numPages = 1`.
Using step 4's `numPages == 1`, xpdf allocates exactly one `Page *` slot and initializes `pages[0] = NULL`. This is the heap region whose left redzone is later read in the crash.
Root cause. Because `doc.getNumPages()` exposes step 4's fallback value 1, this loop executes once with `i == 0` and passes that zero-based value directly into `doc.getLinks(i)`.

Sink. `PDFDoc::getLinks` forwards `page == 0` here. Without any prior `i >= 1 && i <= numPages` check, `i - 1` becomes `-1`, so this condition dereferences one element left of step 5's one-slot `pages` array, matching the saved ASan 8-byte left-out-of-bounds read.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The packaged `patch.diff` only changes FreeType cache headers and the staged metadata names FreeType commits; none of those artifacts touches `xpdf/Catalog.cc`, `xpdf/PDFDoc.cc`, or `build/fuzz_pdfload.cc`, so the packaged patch is unrelated to the witnessed xpdf crash.

format.contract: The saved evidence proves only this exact 79-byte witness with sha256 `c1dfdfccdff22be50e9114cde2a77f0e55ebcc4bfce13d7a3cb36e67add58bfe`. Because `FuzzedDataProvider` pulls integrals from the end of the buffer, the last 25 bytes of this witness are consumed before `ConsumeRemainingBytes<char>()`: 9 bytes for each `ConsumeFloatingPoint<double>()`, 4 bytes for `ConsumeIntegral<int>()`, and 3 bytes for the explicit `ConsumeBool()` calls. In this witness those 25 consumed bytes are all ASCII spaces (`0x20`), so the PDF payload handed to `MemStream` is exactly the first 54 bytes `35 0 obj<</Pages 30 0R\ntrailer<</Root 35 0R 30 0 obj<<`. That prefix is sufficient for xpdf to recover `/Pages 30 0 R`, fetch object 30 as a top Pages dictionary with no integer `/Count`, set `numPages = 1`, and then crash on the first `doc.getLinks(0)` call when `Catalog::getPage` reads `pages[-1]`.
